open_points.subject: _canonical_intake_fingerprint
open_points.text: - _project_expense_intake: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST build the ExpenseIntake from the confirmed publication: recognized_document_id, document_reference, file_ref, document_type, supplier, document_date, currency, total_amount, confirmed_at, contract_version and provenance_ref from the same-named fields of the publication; project_id from the project_id of the authorized context; confirmed_by from the actor_id of that context; and allocations from the allocations argument, the explicit instructions, unchanged. These fields are the intake fingerprint inputs. It MUST NOT project normalized_items or recognition_status of the publication, which are checked at the boundary and then discarded, nor confidence, provider fields or raw responses, which never cross the boundary; actor_kind, key_version, capability and registry_status of the context are authorization facts and are not intake content.
open_points.other_text: - _canonical_intake_fingerprint: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] MUST hash the complete canonical intake independent of input/hash order and exclude clock, actor session, and storage path. The encoding is part of the identity and MUST NOT drift between builds: sorted-key JSON with no insignificant whitespace, enum members as their value, decimals as their plain non-exponential string form, UUIDs and dates as their canonical strings, and allocations sorted by a stable total order over their encoded fields.
open_points.question: Must file_ref be included because every projected field is an intake fingerprint input, or excluded because it is the intake's storage reference?

open_points.subject: _build_expense_aggregate
open_points.text: - _build_expense_aggregate: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The new ExpenseDocument MUST take document_id fresh as the identifier note of this function requires; expense_id from the new Expense; document_reference and file_ref from the same-named fields of the intake, which belong on the document and on no other record; description from the document_type of the intake; client_visible true; created_at from the created_at argument; and updated_at and updated_by None, for the same reason as on the Expense.
open_points.other_text: - ExpenseIntake fields (exact, no others exist): allocations: list[AllocationInstruction], confirmed_at: datetime, confirmed_by: UUID, contract_version: int, currency: str, document_date: date, document_reference: str, document_type: str, file_ref: str, project_id: UUID, provenance_ref: str, recognized_document_id: str, supplier: str, total_amount: Decimal
open_points.question: Must document_reference and file_ref belong only to ExpenseDocument, or must they also be fields of the ExpenseIntake record as declared?
